COMMON JUDGMENT The Petitioners have filed these two petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation Raghavendra Rao.P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 2 for the death of Mr.G.S.Phanibabu and for the injuries sustained by the petitioner Mr.Raghavendra Rao P. in a road traffic accident dated 23.07.2020. Both the petitions have arisen out of a common accident, therefore both the petitions are clubbed together as per order dated 4 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 05.10.2021 and common evidence is led and common judgment is passed. 2. The case of the Petitioners in both the cases is that: On 23.07.2020 at about 7.15pm Mr.G.S.Phanibabu was driving the Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9938 and Mr.Raghavendra Rao P. was an inmate in the same car and they were proceeding on Nice Road, carefully and cautiously, observing all the traffic rules and regulations. When they reached near Anjanapura Lake, Bangalore, the right side front tyre of the Car was punctured. Hence, G.S.Phanibabu parked the Car on the left side of the road by putting all the Car parking lights. Both alighted from the Car, put safety stones around the car. After taking all the safety measures, they started changing the punctured tyre as pedestrians. At that time, all of a sudden the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human 5 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 life from BG Road towards Kengeri side without blowing horn or giving any type of signal, lost control of his Raghavendra Rao. P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 3 motorcycle and hit Mr.G.S.Phanibabu and Mr.Raghavendra Rao and fell down. Due to tremendous impact, Mr.G.S.Phanibabu (in MVC 2854/2020) sustained multiple severe accidental injuries and died on the way to the hospital and Mr.Raghavendra Rao (in MVC 2855/2020) also sustained multiple severe accidental injuries on his head region, chest region, hands and other parts of the body. Hence, his total income is Rs.26,60,255/ per annum from both the companies. Prior to the accident, the deceased G.S.Phanibabu was hale and healthy, the only bread earner of the entire family. Due to his sudden death the deceased's wife and children have been deprived of the Raghavendra Rao. P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 4 contribution which the deceased was making towards the entire family. Due to accidental injuries he was not able to attend to his Job regularly. So, he lost that income. 5. Therefore, the Respondents 1 & 2 being the insurer and the Owner of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to them. Hence this petition. 6. In response to service of notice issued by this court/Tribunal, the Respondent No.1 has appeared and filed written statement. In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent No.2 did not appear in MVC 2854/2020. Hence, placed exparte. In MVC 2855/2020, the Raghavendra Rao. P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 5 8 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them. 8. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri. G.S.Phanibabu? If so from whom and to what extent? 3. What Order or Award? 9. But in the case on hand it is to be noted that the deceased had joined the ALS Testing company only in the month of the accident. Ex.P.24 appointment letter is dated 20.07.2020 and the appointment is effective from 06.07.2020. The final settlement statement at Ex.P.25 shows the date of joining as 06.07.2020. With respect of Trans Tools Corporation, as per Ex.P.12 ledger account and the statement, the deceased was receiving Rs.75,000/ + Travel allowance of around Rs.15,000/ from April 2019. As per Ex.P.26 the Gross monthly salary of the deceased in ALS Testing 27 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 Services India was Rs.1,02,055/. Therefore, the total of Rs.75,000/ + Rs.1,02,055/ = Rs.1,77,055/ amount is considered as the monthly income of the deceased. The annual income comes to Rs.21,24,660/. If the professional tax of the deceased is deducted to get his annual taxable income, it comes to Rs.21,22,260/ per annum. Standard Deduction for the year 202021 was Rs.50,000/ so the taxable income comes to Rs.20,72,260/. 19. texts.facts: There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. Further the alleged accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself. However, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Helen's Case referred supra, unless the benefits are exclusively for accidental death, the benefits given like family benefit, PF, life insurance, group insurance, house rent and exgratia cannot be deducted from the compensation.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the petitioner has relied on (1) 2009 (II) ACC 444 Supreme Court of India: Bimladevi & Ors. And (3). 2021 ACJ 17 Supreme Court of India: Anita Sharma & Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr., wherein the courts have held that the claimants have to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability. Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and Raghavendra Rao. P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 14 Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability. In support of the same, he has relied on (1) 2017 ACJ 1149 High Court of Delhi: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. R.K.Arora & Ors. And (2) 2021 21 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased is 13. , employees keep changing their companies for better remuneration. Therefore it can be safely assumed that the deceased was not a permanent employee and as per Pranay Sethi Case an addition of 25% to his income as future prospects should be made since the deceased is less than 50 years old. Therefore, the Raghavendra Rao.P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 The Petitioner is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 43 years and she has to live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ under the head of loss of consortium. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate. The Respondent No.1 has contended that the Two wheeler rider did not have a valid and effective DL. But has not led any evidence and hence it is clear that the respondents have failed to prove their defence.
